title: Autonomic Pacing & Rollback Orchestrator for SLO-Aware Cost Tuning
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Build an autonomic orchestration layer that can safely apply cost-optimizing batching and KV-cache configs while enforcing latency and throughput SLO guardrails. The system will: 1) propose candidate config changes (batch size targets, prefetch windows, cache TTLs, quantization hints) from Optimize recommendations, 2) stage and apply profiles to cohorts, 3) continuously evaluate SLO signals and rollback automatically on anomalies, and 4) provide deterministic, auditable runbook steps for on-call. This ticket focuses on the control-plane components: the pacing controller (paces config ramps using a configurable curve and confidence bands), the lightweight anomaly detector (multi-metric, cohort-aware), and the transactional rollback orchestrator (two-phase apply with snapshot + rollback tombstone).
motivation: We frequently see safe cost wins stalled because config rollouts trigger non-deterministic latency regressions in tail percentiles. Manual rollouts are slow and error-prone. An autonomic operator that understands SLOs, cohorts, and risk budgets will accelerate cost capture without compromising reliability.
design_overview: Key subcomponents: 1) Pacing controller: uses a sigmoid ramp with per-cohort rate limits and dynamic backoff when SLO pressure grows; 2) Cohort router: SLO-aware routing layer that can route degraded traffic to a conservative variant (lower batch, disabled prefetch) by policy; 3) Anomaly detector: combines EWMA on p50/p95/p99, rolling percentile sketches for tail, and a drift detector that uses permutation testing over recent windows; 4) Transactional apply: two-phase commit for config with canary->ramp->global stages and atomic rollback tombstones; 5) Observability: per-config tracing, token-level cost delta, and a dedicated dashboard tile for active experiments.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike, 1 week): prototype pacing controller and cohort router in staging using existing feature-flag hooks. Phase 2 (2 weeks): implement anomaly detector, integrate with metrics pipeline (Prometheus + ClickHouse sketches), add canary mechanics. Phase 3 (2 weeks): build transactional apply/rollback with metadata snapshots and test harness for deterministic failure injection. Phase 4 (1 week): integrate with Optimize recommender and Redwood Console rollout UI. Final: on-call runbook + playbooks.
acceptance_criteria: Can stage a candidate batching/caching profile to a 1% canary cohort and auto-ramp to 25% using the pacing curve without manual intervention
System detects injected latency regressions (p99 increase > 25% or absolute > 250ms) in canary and performs automated rollback within configured SLAs
SLO-aware router routes > 95% of affected traffic to safe variant during an active anomaly and returns traffic after SLO recovery
All config changes produce an immutable audit entry with before/after snapshots and a reference to the Optimize recommendation
End-to-end tests simulate network/cold-cache scenarios and show no data corruption after rollback
risks_and_mitigations: False positives from anomaly detector: mitigate by requiring multi-metric confirmation and minimum sample-size before rollback
Cohort starvation during rollouts: mitigate by ensuring minimum throughput floor and progressive ramping
Rollback flapping: implement cooldown windows and progressive backoff to avoid oscillation
Observability gaps: add synthetic workload harness and replay capability to reproduce regressions

open_questions: What is the default cohort sizing heuristic for low-traffic tenants? (suggested: min 100 qps or 1% whichever larger)
Should rollback be immediate or allow a short quiesce period to reduce false-positive flaps? (proposal: require 2 consecutive anomaly windows or immediate if p99>500ms)
Do we expose advanced pacing knobs to customers or keep them internal until stable?
